title: Annotatio V §.II open: antiquity’s double true eating — proper/improper, corporal/spiritual — for double food
pass_a_gloss: §. II. That a double Eating in the Sacred Supper — Proper and Improper, Corporal and Spiritual, each equally true — has been enjoined on us by the Institutor of the Sacred Supper on account of the double food exhibited there, proper and improper, Corporal and Spiritual, equally true on both sides, namely bread and Christ’s Body: this pious antiquity has always believed.
pass_b_english: §.II: pious antiquity always held that the Sacred Supper enjoins a double eating — Proper and Improper, Corporal and Spiritual — each equally true.
The reason is the double food exhibited there, equally true on both sides: bread and Christ’s Body, from the Supper’s Institutor.
source_text: §. II. Manducationem in S. Cœna duplicem, Propriam & Impropriam, Corporalem & Spiritualem, utramque æquè veram, ob duplicem inibì exhibitum proprium & improprium, Corporalem & Spiritualem, æquè verum utrobique cibum, panem nempe & Corpus Christi, ab Institutore S. Cœnæ, injunctam nobis esse, pia semper credidit antiquitas.
notes: §.II open: double true eating for double food.
